label: Copy-phase update gate (after first output), biased toward certain input tokens and short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens or the <DEL> step, and almost never at recall_idx 0 or 1 (recall_idx>=2 holds 93% of mass). It is only active on about 12% of copy steps, though, and which ones is not cleanly captured. The rate is higher when the fed-back input is one of a token subset (2, u, g, h, n, w, z, ...), for short sequences (L=3 at 32%, L=4 at 10%), and at certain absolute timesteps (t=6, 11-12, 17), which suggests a mix of a clock and token identity. The strongest activations are L=3 sequences at the last copy steps whose input is u or 2. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.005). The best predicate reaches F1 of about 0.36, with high mass recall (0.85) but low precision (0.23).
